travel_tips.tip: Use the Islamabad Expressway to move quickly between the airport, Rawalpindi, and central sectors, avoiding sector-internal roads.
Islamabad's sector-based grid layout (F-6, F-7, G-9, etc.) can be confusing for first-time visitors -- ride-hailing apps handle navigation well.
Islamabad is generally one of Pakistan's safer and more orderly cities for tourists, but standard city precautions still apply in busy markets.
Visit Daman-e-Koh and Faisal Mosque in the late afternoon for the best light and cooler temperatures, especially in summer.

history.founded: A planned city, purpose-built starting in the 1960s to replace Karachi as Pakistan's capital
history.city_history: Islamabad was designed by Greek architect Constantinos Doxiadis as a modern, sector-based planned city, officially becoming Pakistan's capital in 1967. Unlike Pakistan's older cities, it has relatively little ancient history itself, but sits near the historic Taxila region, one of the great centers of ancient learning on the Silk Road.
history.province_history: As a federal territory rather than a province, Islamabad was carved out specifically to serve as Pakistan's capital, chosen partly for its central location and proximity to the military headquarters in Rawalpindi.
